kept.excerpt: In the Democratic primary in New Hampshire's First Congressional District, Maura Sullivan and Stefany Shaheen are statistically tied, followed by Carleigh Beriont. Hollie Noveletsky and Anthony DiLorenzo are also statistically tied on the Republican side.
kept.publisher: University of New Hampshire Survey Center
kept.relevance: The pollster's dated release establishes that the Republican nomination contest was statistically tied at the evidence cutoff.

kept.excerpt: Also on the Republican side, veteran, nurse, and business owner Hollie Noveletsky has 28% support, while Portsmouth businessman Anthony DiLorenzo is at 25%. Manchester state Rep. Brian Cole trails at 7%, while 38% remain undecided. DiLorenzo has President Donald Trump’s endorsement and a significant fundraising advantage, but Noveletsky narrowly led him in the UNH survey.
kept.relevance: This contemporaneous report supplies the cutoff-day polling numbers, the large undecided share, and DiLorenzo's endorsement and financial advantages.

kept.excerpt: Anthony DiLorenzo leads Hollie Noveletsky 30%-17% in the Republican primary. These results are from a Saint Anselm College Survey Center poll based on online surveys of 1411 New Hampshire likely voters. Surveys were collected between August 17th and 18th, 2026, from cell phone users randomly drawn from a sample of registered voters reflecting the demographic and partisan characteristics of the voting population.
kept.publisher: Saint Anselm College / New Hampshire Institute of Politics
kept.relevance: An independent poll released shortly before the cutoff shows a substantially different ordering from UNH, making polling disagreement material to the forecast.

kept.excerpt: Hollie Noveletsky, Anthony DiLorenzo, and Brian Cole, all candidates in the Republican race for the state’s 1st Congressional District, declined. With the candidates largely in line with the Trump administration on issues big and small, they are instead touting their business records, biographies and professional accomplishments.
kept.publisher: New Hampshire Public Radio, syndicated by Maine Public
kept.relevance: Reporting from the August 13 debate identifies the active leading competitors and explains the limited policy differentiation among them.

kept.excerpt: President Donald Trump is endorsing Anthony DiLorenzo in New Hampshire’s 1st Congressional District race.
kept.relevance: Trump's endorsement of Noveletsky's principal rival is an important Republican-primary signal known before the cutoff.

kept.excerpt: The NH-01 GOP primary debate will be held at the New Hampshire Institute of Politics auditorium on Wednesday, August 26 at 6:00 p.m. Rep. Brian Cole, Anthony DiLorenzo and Hollie Noveletsky have all confirmed their participation. The debates will not open to the general public, but they will be broadcast live on Manchester Public TV channel 16 and will stream online as well.
kept.relevance: The dated organizer announcement documents a scheduled cutoff-day campaign event and confirms participation by the three main Republican contenders.

kept.excerpt: Manchester, NH – Former Manchester Mayor and Former Executive Councilor for District 4, Ted Gatsas, has weighed into the GOP Primary for NH CD-1 with an endorsement for conservative CEO and Army Reserve veteran Hollie Noveletsky. Noveletsky’s campaign has built a durable coalition behind her with almost 90 endorsements ranging from political figures, like Congresswoman Virginia Foxx and NH Senate Majority Leader Regina Birdsell, to leading organizations like Maggie’s List, the Associated Builders and Contractors (ABC) NH/VT Chapter, and the Associated General Contractors of America PAC (AGC PAC).
kept.relevance: This official campaign release documents Noveletsky's claimed Republican and industry support network, with the endorsement count treated as a campaign claim.

search_notes: Frozen evidence cutoff: 2026-08-26, inclusive. Included only sources with explicit publication dates on or before the cutoff; excluded later reporting, undated live profiles, election-result pages, and prediction-market or betting material. Source text and dates were verified through web_search results and targeted searches. Direct web_fetch failed because of provider configuration; the requested agent-reach web-read fallback was rate-limited, so full-page retrieval was unavailable. Excerpts reproduce factual source sentences available in search results; no post-cutoff developments were used. The NHJournal debate announcement displays July 20 publication and July 21 update dates, both before the cutoff. The Saint Anselm sample size quoted is for its overall statewide survey, not the NH-01 Republican subsample. Campaign endorsement claims are attributed to the campaign and are not independent verification.
